Instead of needing multiple download links or QR codes for your app, you only need one smart download short link (or QR code) from Onelink.to.

You add the download links to Google Play, Apple App Store, etc; and we make sure to send each user clicking the smart Onelink.to link (or scanning the QR code) to the correct app store/marketplace depending on what device is being used. Or to your homepage or similar if it is not a mobile device (using a "Fallback URL").

Onelink.to launched in 2011 and is one of the first services offering smart download links.`],tags:[`onelink`]},{id:`what-is-a-onelink`,redirect_from:[`what-is-an-onelink`],title:`What is a Onelink from Onelink.to?`,content:[`A Onelink is a smart download short link from Onelink.to. With a Onelink you only need one link or QR code to all app stores. There is no need to print multiple QR codes, or have multiple download links in your email marketing. We will make sure to send the user to the correct app store / marketplace based on the device used.

Another great thing with a Onelink is that it is a dynamic short link, meaning that you can change your app download links at any time, without your Onelink changing. Onelink.to will automatically send each user to App Store or Google Play etc, depending on what device is being used. On top of that you get a dynamic link and QR code, and statistics.

The use cases are numerous, but the most common are:
<ul><li>Email and SMS marketing and direct messaging</li><li>Web based banner or link advertising using shortlinks</li><li>Printed advertising with QR codes, in newspapers, outdoor advertising, etc</li><li>Digital signage advertising with QR codes</li><li>App download shortcuts in printed material (manuals, product sheets, etc) using QR codes</li></ul>Try creating a Onelink today, start free.`],tags:[`onelink`,`qr code`]}]},{id:`faq-onelink-howto`,faqlang:`en`,title:`How to work with Onelinks`,items:[{id:`how-do-i-create-a-onelink`,redirect_from:[`how-do-i-create-an-onelink`],title:`How do I create a Onelink?`,content:[`Sign up for a free or paid account, then choose <strong>Create new Onelink</strong> on the My Onelinks page and add your App Store and Google Play links. The Onelink's short link and QR code are ready to use straight away.

Click on the Onelink you want to edit, then update the App Store URLs, Google Play URLs, Fallback URL, etc. Changes normally reach all Onelink.to servers within 5 minutes.`],tags:[`edit`,`management`]},{id:`how-long-do-changes-take`,title:`How long do changes to my Onelink take to apply?`,content:[`When you update your Onelink destinations or settings, changes normally reach all Onelink.to servers within 5 minutes.`],tags:[`edit`,`propagation`,`timing`]},{id:`where-is-the-app-name-shown`,title:`Where is my app name shown?`,content:[`Add it per Onelink in the Onelink editor, under <strong>Name your Onelink and app</strong>. It is shown exactly as you type it, in every language:

<ul><li>in the header and browser tab of the pages visitors see when they are not sent straight to a store, such as on a computer without a link of its own — in place of the Onelink.to name</li><li>on the page Android visitors see before Google Play opens, and as its browser tab title — only when <strong>Also on Android</strong> is ticked under <strong>After the store</strong> (see <a href="/features/after-the-store">After the store</a>)</li></ul>`],tags:[`edit`,`work with onelinks`]},{id:`print-a-qr-code-before-your-app-launches`,title:`Can I print a QR code before my app is in the stores?`,content:[`Yes. Create a Onelink with only the fallback link, pointing to a page about the upcoming app, and print or publish its QR code and link. On launch day, add the App Store and Google Play links. Every printed code then sends phone users to the stores, normally within 5 minutes.`],tags:[`edit`,`launch`]},{id:`delete-onelink`,title:`Can I delete a Onelink?`,content:[`Yes, you can delete a Onelink from the My Onelinks page, but be careful: once deleted, the link no longer works. On onelink.to, visitors see a page saying the Onelink does not exist; on a custom domain, the domain's <strong>When no Onelink matches</strong> setting decides where they go. Consider any printed materials or campaigns that use the link.`],tags:[`delete`,`management`]}]},{id:`faq-my-onelink-account`,faqlang:`en`,title:`My Onelink.to Account`,short_title:`My Account`,items:[{id:`sign-in-with-google-or-microsoft-account`,title:`Can I sign in with my Google or Microsoft account?`,content:[`Yes. You can sign up for and log in to Onelink.to using your existing Google or Microsoft account — no separate password required.

On the Login or Sign Up page, click the <strong>Sign in with Google</strong> or <strong>Sign in with Microsoft</strong> button and authorize Onelink.to to access your basic account information. We use this only to identify you on subsequent logins.`],tags:[`account`,`login`]},{id:`google-or-microsoft-email-address-has-changed`,title:`My Google or Microsoft email address has changed, what do I do?`,content:[`Did you register using Google or Microsoft Sign Up and now that email address has changed?

As long as you still can receive emails on the original email address there is a solution.

1. Generate a password for your old email address by clicking the "Forgot Password" button on the Login page.

2. When the new password is set and you are logged in, go to <strong>Settings</strong> > <strong>Profile</strong> and change the email to your new Google or Microsoft email address.

After the email is updated you can log in using Google or Microsoft and your new email address.`],tags:[`email address`,`account`],redirect_from:[`google-email-address-has-changed`]},{id:`multiple-users-on-same-account`,title:`Can my colleague and I use the same account?`,content:[`Yes. Please send us an email on support@onelink.to and we'll do our best to help.`],tags:[`onelink`]},{id:`can-i-use-two-factor-authentication`,title:`Can I use Two-Factor Authentication on my account?`,content:[`On our paid plans we support Two-Factor Authentication (TFA/2FA) with Time-based One-Time Passwords (TOTP), which require an authenticator app such as Google Authenticator or Authy, or a password manager that supports them.

TFA applies when you log in with a password. When you log in with Google or Microsoft, the protection of that account applies instead.

Turn on TFA under <strong>Settings</strong> > <strong>Login Security</strong>.`],tags:[`account`]}]},{id:`faq-subscriptions-and-payments`,faqlang:`en`,title:`Subscriptions and Payments`,short_title:`Subscriptions`,items:[{id:`difference-between-plans`,title:`What is the difference between the plans?`,content:[`The plans differ in how many Onelinks and users they include, how long statistics are kept, and which features they have, such as custom links, invisible redirects, detailed statistics, custom domains and the Stats API.

See the full comparison on the <a href="/pricing">pricing page</a>, and what each feature does in the <a href="/features">feature guides</a>.`],tags:[`pricing`,`plans`]},{id:`how-to-upgrade-plan`,title:`How do I upgrade my plan?`,content:[`Choose <strong>Upgrade Plan</strong> in the top menu, or go to <strong>Settings</strong> > <strong>Subscription</strong>. Select your new plan and complete the payment. Upgrades take effect immediately, and the remainder of your current plan is credited towards the new one.`],tags:[`pricing`,`upgrade`]},{id:`what-happens-after-1000-clicks-free-plan`,title:`What happens after I reach 1,000 clicks on the free plan?`,content:[`From three months after you sign up, the Free plan includes 1,000 invisible redirects a month. After that, your Onelinks still work, but visitors see a Onelink.to page that forwards them to the destination after a short delay, or at once if they tap the button. Traffic itself is unlimited, and the count starts again on the first of each month.

See <a href="/features/invisible-redirects">Invisible redirects</a>.`],tags:[`pricing`,`free plan`,`clicks`]},{id:`is-onelink-to-ad-free`,title:`Is Onelink.to ad-free?`,content:[`Yes, Onelink.to is ad-free on every plan, including the Free plan. Onelink.to never shows ads to people who click your Onelinks or scan your QR codes.`],tags:[`pricing`,`ads`]}]},{id:`faq-onelink-statistics`,faqlang:`en`,title:`Onelink Statistics`,items:[{id:`what-statistics-is-available-from-the-onelink-usage`,title:`What statistics is available from the Onelink usage?`,content:[`Every click and QR code scan is counted.

All plans
• Device statistics: clicks per device type (iPhone, Android, etc).

Professional plan and up
• Redirect statistics: where each visitor was sent.
• Referring domains: which website the click came from.
• Country statistics: where the click came from.

Team plan and up
• UTM statistics: clicks per UTM tag.

See <a href="/features/statistics">Statistics</a>.`],tags:[`statistics`]},{id:`what-is-utm-tracking`,title:`What is UTM tracking?`,content:[`UTM tags are labels at the end of a link that say where it was shared, such as <code>https://onelink.to/mycode?utm_source=email&utm_campaign=50-percent-off</code>. The names are always the five standard ones: <code>utm_source</code>, <code>utm_medium</code>, <code>utm_campaign</code>, <code>utm_term</code> and <code>utm_content</code>.

On the Team plan and up, your statistics show the clicks per tag. See <a href="/features/statistics#statsUTM">UTM campaigns</a>.`],tags:[`statistics`]},{id:`how-do-i-use-utm-tracking-with-onelink-to`,title:`How do I use UTM tracking with Onelink.to?`,content:[`Add UTM tags to your Onelink before you share it, by hand or with the UTM campaign tool: open a Onelink and choose <strong>Create UTM campaign</strong>. Only clicks on the tagged link or QR code are counted by tag, so use the tagged version wherever you publish it.

See the step-by-step guide in <a href="/guides/track-a-campaign">Track a campaign</a>.`],tags:[`statistics`]},{id:`can-i-access-statistics-via-api`,title:`Can I access my click statistics via an API?`,content:[`Yes. The Stats API is available on the Team Plus and Enterprise plans, and gives your own tools the device, redirect, country, referrer and UTM statistics of all your Onelinks. The full reference is under <strong>Settings</strong> > <strong>Stats API</strong>.

On many mobile phones, you can scan a QR code directly in the camera app, or by using a downloaded QR scanner app, making them very easy to interact with.`],tags:[`qr code`]},{id:`what-is-a-dynamic-qr-code`,title:`What is a dynamic QR code?`,content:[`A Dynamic QR code is essentially the same as a regular QR code. The difference is that instead of having the QR code contain the target content, like a web link, it contains a short link that leads you to the target content. The main benefit is that this makes the QR code action changable, i.e. dynamic. Another benefit is that you can find out how many persons scan your QR code.`],tags:[`qr code`,`short link`]},{id:`what-is-a-short-link`,title:`What is a short link?`,content:[`A short link is like a shortcut for the web. A regular link to some specific content on the web is normally pretty long and sometimes unpractical to share. An URL shortener (service) handles that problem by wrapping the original long link in a short link package. When someone click the short link, the browser will first go to the URL shortener service and then bounce to the original link (target URL).

If you are able to edit the target URL, you have a dynamic short link, which is great for printed QR codes. Another benefit is that you can find out how many persons click your link, if you can't track the original link.`],tags:[`short link`]},{id:`what-is-a-dynamic-short-link`,title:`What is a dynamic short link?`,content:[`A dynamic short link is a short link where you can edit the target URL without the short link changing. This is great for printed QR codes.`],tags:[`short link`]},{id:`what-is-a-smart-short-link`,title:`What is a smart short link?`,content:[`A smart short link is designed to be more versatile and dynamic than a regular short link. Both provide a shortened version of an URL, but a smart short link allows for much more functionality. It allows the creator of the link to track clicks, redirect users to different pages based on their device or location, and provide additional functionality such as analytics and A/B testing.

A regular short link, on the other hand, is simply a shortened version of a URL that redirects users to the original website or page. It does not provide any additional functionality beyond redirecting users to the original link.

Smart short links also have the ability to redirect the user to the correct app store or website depending on the user's device, for example a smart link can redirect an iPhone user to the Apple App Store and an android user to the Google Play Store.

They are often used in marketing campaigns to track the effectiveness of different marketing efforts and to optimize the user experience.

Smart short links are often dynamic where you can edit the target URL without the short link changing. This is great for printed QR codes.`],tags:[`short link`]},{id:`what-is-an-url-shortener`,title:`What is an URL shortener?`,content:[`An URL shortener is a service where you can create short links and possibly dynamic short links. All your Onelinks work with any of your verified custom domains.`],tags:[`custom domains`,`plans`,`pricing`]},{id:`how-to-setup-custom-domain`,title:`How do I set up a custom domain?`,content:[`Choose a subdomain such as <code>app.example.com</code>, add it under <strong>Settings</strong> > <strong>Custom Domains</strong>, add a <strong>CNAME</strong> record pointing it to <code>mydomain.onelink.to</code> where your domain is managed, and choose <strong>Setup Domain</strong>. You get an email when the domain is ready.

See the step-by-step guide in <a href="/guides/set-up-a-custom-domain">Set up a custom domain</a>.`],tags:[`custom domains`,`setup`,`dns`]},{id:`custom-domain-cloudflare-proxy`,title:`My CNAME looks correct but verification fails (Cloudflare)`,content:[`If you use <strong>Cloudflare</strong>, make sure your CNAME record is set to <strong>DNS only</strong> (the grey cloud icon) and <strong>not Proxied</strong> (the orange cloud icon).

When a record is proxied, Cloudflare hides your CNAME and serves traffic through its own servers, so we can't see that the record points to <code>mydomain.onelink.to</code>, and can't verify your domain or issue its TLS certificate. Open your Cloudflare DNS settings, find the record for your subdomain, and click the orange cloud so it turns grey. Onelink.to checks the record again about every hour, so verification then completes by itself.

The same applies to other proxy, CDN, or web-firewall services (such as Sucuri, Imperva, or StackPath): disable proxying for this record.`],tags:[`custom domains`,`dns`,`cloudflare`,`troubleshooting`]},{id:`custom-domain-with-cloudflare`,title:`Can I use Cloudflare (or another CDN) with my custom domain?`,content:[`Yes. You can keep your domain on Cloudflare, Sucuri, Imperva, StackPath, or any other DNS/CDN provider and still use it as a custom domain with Onelink.to. There is just one important setting.

For the specific CNAME record that points your subdomain (e.g. <code>app.example.com</code>) to <code>mydomain.onelink.to</code>, you must <strong>disable proxying</strong> on that record. In Cloudflare this means setting the record to <strong>DNS only</strong> (grey cloud), not <strong>Proxied</strong> (orange cloud). Other providers have similar toggles.

This only affects the one CNAME record for your Onelink subdomain. Your root domain and any other records can stay proxied as before, so the rest of your site continues to benefit from your CDN/WAF. We handle TLS termination and traffic for the Onelink subdomain on our side.`],tags:[`custom domains`,`dns`,`cloudflare`,`cdn`,`proxy`]},{id:`custom-domain-caa-records`,title:`What if my domain has CAA records?`,content:[`<strong>CAA</strong> (Certification Authority Authorization) is an optional DNS record that tells certificate authorities which providers are allowed to issue TLS certificates for your domain. Most domains do not have CAA records, in which case there is nothing to do — TLS issuance for your Onelink subdomain will just work.

If your root domain <em>does</em> have CAA records, you must explicitly allow <strong>Let's Encrypt</strong>, which is the certificate authority we use. Add the following entry alongside your existing CAA records, on the subdomain you're using with Onelink.to:
<ul><li>Type: <code>CAA</code></li><li>Name: your subdomain (e.g. <code>app</code>)</li><li>Data: <code>0 issue "letsencrypt.org"</code></li><li>TTL: <code>3600</code> (or Auto)</li></ul>

Not sure if your domain has CAA records? Open your DNS provider's dashboard and look for any entries of type CAA on the root domain. If there are none, you can skip this step entirely. If there are, add the entry above before clicking "Setup Domain" — otherwise certificate issuance will fail and verification will not complete.`],tags:[`custom domains`,`dns`,`caa`,`tls`,`certificates`]},{id:`can-i-use-root-domain`,title:`Can I use a root domain (example.com)?`,content:[`No, you must use a subdomain like <code>app.example.com</code> or <code>link.example.com</code>. Root domains (e.g., <code>example.com</code>) cannot be used because they don't support CNAME records, which are required for custom domain setup.`],tags:[`custom domains`,`dns`,`subdomain`]},{id:`custom-domain-bare-redirect`,title:`Where does my custom domain send visitors when no Onelink matches?`,content:[`Two situations each get their own answer:
<ul><li><strong>The domain on its own</strong> - for example <code>app.example.com</code> with nothing after the slash</li><li><strong>A link that does not exist</strong> - mistyped, deleted or never created, like <code>app.example.com/oldcampaign</code>. Longer paths such as <code>app.example.com/product/123</code> follow the same choice</li></ul>
For each, choose one of:
<ul><li><strong>Show a not-found page</strong></li><li><strong>Send them to your web address</strong> - a page on your own site, such as your homepage</li><li><strong>Send them to a default Onelink</strong> - one of your Onelinks, so visitors still reach the right app store</li></ul>
Set this under <strong>Settings > Custom Domains</strong>, in the domain's <strong>When no Onelink matches</strong> section. Add the web address or choose the default Onelink first: a choice can only name a destination the domain has.

When a link that does not exist goes to your web address, you also decide what happens to the path: drop it, let it replace the web address's path, or add it to that path - so <code>app.example.com/product/123</code> can land on the matching page of your site.

The web address must be a full <code>http</code> or <code>https</code> URL and cannot point back to the same custom domain. Links that match one of your Onelinks always go to that Onelink's destinations.`],tags:[`custom domains`,`redirect`,`bare domain`,`not found`,`default onelink`,`web address`,`settings`]},{id:`custom-domain-verification-time`,title:`How long does domain verification take?`,content:[`Usually within an hour of adding the DNS record. Onelink.to checks the record when you choose <strong>Setup Domain</strong> and then about every hour; once it is found, the TLS certificate is issued within minutes, and you get an email when the domain is ready.

If the record is still wrong after about seven hours, you get an email instead: fix the record, then choose <strong>Setup Domain</strong> again. See <a href="/guides/set-up-a-custom-domain">Set up a custom domain</a>.`],tags:[`custom domains`,`timing`,`dns`,`tls`]},{id:`tls-certificates-included`,title:`Are TLS certificates included?`,content:[`Yes! TLS certificates are automatically generated and managed for all custom domains using <strong>Let's Encrypt</strong>. Certificates are valid for 90 days and are automatically renewed before expiration. You don't need to do anything - the entire process is handled automatically by Onelink.to.`],tags:[`custom domains`,`tls`,`security`,`certificates`]},{id:`deleting-custom-domain-impact`,title:`What happens to my links if I delete a custom domain?`,content:[`<strong>Warning:</strong> Deleting a custom domain will immediately break any existing links or QR codes that use that domain. Anyone clicking those links will see an error.

Before deleting a domain:
<ul><li>Update any Onelinks that are using the domain as their default</li><li>Update or replace any QR codes that display the domain</li><li>Consider the impact on printed materials, marketing campaigns, and any other places where the links are used</li></ul>

All your Onelinks will continue to work through <code>onelink.to</code> and any other custom domains you have configured.`],tags:[`custom domains`,`delete`,`management`]}]},{id:`faq-open-in-app`,faqlang:`en`,title:`Opening your app (deep linking)`,short_title:`Open in app`,items:[{id:`what-is-deep-linking`,related:[],title:`What is deep linking?`,content:[`A deep link is an ordinary web address that opens your app when it is installed, and the web page when it is not.

On iOS the mechanism is <strong>Universal Links</strong>, on Android <strong>App Links</strong>: your domain hosts a small file naming the apps allowed to open its links, and your app declares the domain.

Onelink.to uses deep linking to build open-app-or-download: instead of opening a web page if the app is not installed, a Onelink sends the visitor to download your app.`],tags:[`app links`,`universal links`,`deep links`,`deep linking`,`onelink`,`open in app`]},{id:`what-is-an-open-app-or-download-link`,related:[],title:`What is an open-app-or-download link?`,content:[`A link that opens your app when it is installed, and sends everyone else to download it — to the right app store for their device, or wherever else that Onelink points.

It is available on the <strong>Team Plus</strong> and <strong>Enterprise</strong> plans, and is set up on your custom domain.

On Android, the link can also reach your app through an install from Google Play — see <a href="/what-is-deferred-deep-linking">What is deferred deep linking?</a>`],tags:[`deep linking`,`deferred deep linking`,`onelink`,`app store`,`download`,`open in app`]},{id:`what-is-deferred-deep-linking`,related:[],title:`What is deferred deep linking?`,content:[`A link that opens your app on the content it points to even when the app has to be installed first: a new user taps it, installs the app, and lands on that content instead of the start screen.

Onelink.to does this on Android with the <strong>Google Play Install Referrer API</strong>: the Onelink adds the tapped link to the Google Play address, Google Play keeps it through the install, and your app reads it on first launch. No SDK is required, only a few lines of code in your app. Apple provides no similar technology, so this works on Android only.

It is available on the <strong>Team</strong> plan and above. See the step-by-step guide in <a href="/guides/deferred-deep-linking-android">Deferred deep linking on Android</a>.`],tags:[`deep linking`,`deferred deep linking`,`android`,`google play`,`install referrer`,`developers`,`open in app`]},{id:`open-in-app-requires-custom-domain`,related:[`what-are-custom-domains`,`how-to-setup-custom-domain`],title:`Why does deep linking require a custom domain?`,content:[`Apple and Google both verify that the domain and the app belong to the same owner. This stops anyone else from making links on their domain open your app.`],tags:[`app links`,`custom domains`,`plans`]},{id:`which-plans-include-open-in-app`,related:[],title:`Which plans include deep linking?`,content:[`The <strong>Team Plus</strong> and <strong>Enterprise</strong> plans, which are the plans with custom domains — Team Plus covers 1 domain, Enterprise up to 3. There is no limit on how many apps a domain may open: a bank with separate retail and business apps can point both at one domain.`],tags:[`app links`,`plans`,`pricing`]},{id:`how-to-set-up-open-in-app`,related:[`how-to-setup-custom-domain`],title:`How do I set up deep linking?`,content:[`Two halves. The second belongs to whoever builds your app. See the step-by-step guide in <a href="/guides/open-links-in-your-app">Open links in your app (deep linking)</a>.

<strong>On Onelink.to:</strong>
<ol><li>Set up your custom domain, if you have not already</li><li>Open <strong>Settings > Custom Domains</strong> and expand the domain</li><li>Under <strong>Open in app</strong>, upload the association file for each platform — we check it and point out anything that looks wrong</li></ol>

<strong>In your app:</strong>
<ul><li><strong>iOS:</strong> an Associated Domains entitlement for <code>applinks:app.example.com</code> — <a href="https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode/supporting-associated-domains" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Supporting associated domains</a>. To test without waiting for Apple's CDN, append <code>?mode=developer</code> and enable Developer Mode on the device</li><li><strong>Android:</strong> an intent filter for the domain with <code>android:autoVerify="true"</code> — <a href="https://developer.android.com/training/app-links/verify-android-applinks" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Verify Android App Links</a>. The fingerprint must be the SHA-256 of the <strong>Play App Signing</strong> certificate, not the upload key — <a href="https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9842756" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Play App Signing</a>. Check a device with <code>adb shell pm verify-app-links --re-verify your.package.name</code></li></ul>

Both need a new build submitted to the stores, so plan this with your app release.`],tags:[`app links`,`deep linking`,`setup`,`ios`,`android`,`developers`,`open in app`]},{id:`where-do-i-get-the-association-files`,related:[],title:`Where do I get assetlinks.json and the AASA file?`,content:[`<strong>Android:</strong> Play Console shows a complete <code>assetlinks.json</code> for your app, on its <strong>App integrity</strong> page under App signing. Upload that file.

<strong>iOS:</strong> Apple ships no generator. You need your <strong>App ID Prefix</strong> (10 characters, under Membership on developer.apple.com — usually, but not always, your Team ID) and your app's <strong>Bundle ID</strong> from Xcode. We build the file from those and show it before you save it.

See the step-by-step guide in <a href="/guides/open-links-in-your-app">Open links in your app (deep linking)</a>.`],tags:[`app links`,`setup`,`ios`,`android`,`files`]},{id:`open-in-app-not-working`,related:[],title:`Why does my link open the browser, not the app?`,content:[`In order of likelihood:

<ul><li><strong>The app build has not shipped.</strong> The app half takes effect only once the new version is on the device</li><li><strong>The wrong Android fingerprint.</strong> It must be the SHA-256 of your <strong>Play App Signing</strong> certificate, not your upload key. It fails silently</li><li><strong>The device has an old copy.</strong> Phones fetch the association when the app is installed or updated, so test on a fresh install</li><li><strong>Apple has not caught up.</strong> Apple collects the iOS file through its own CDN, so a change can take up to a day to reach devices</li></ul>`],tags:[`app links`,`troubleshooting`,`not working`]},{id:`open-in-app-and-statistics`,related:[],title:`Do deep links still count clicks?`,content:[`Not for the visitors whose app opens. When the phone hands a link straight to your app, the request never reaches Onelink.to.

Clicks are still counted for everyone else: visitors without the app, everyone on desktop, and links opened in apps that do not support the mechanism.
